title: Chapter 10 summary and quiz
recap: Combine range validation, domain aliases, and deliberate conversion points into one small API. Validate inputs before arithmetic and keep integer money calculations wide enough.
Rounding at the wrong stage changes a bill: discounting each item then multiplying is not necessarily the same as discounting the full subtotal once. The contract specifies the latter.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement invoiceTotal(unitPrice, quantity, discountPercent) in integer Cents and currencyUnits(cents) as double major units. Invoice total is unitPrice*quantity*(100-discountPercent)/100, truncating fractional cents only at the end. Negative unitPrice/quantity or discount outside [0,100] returns -1; zero quantity is valid. Inputs are unitPrice <= 1000000 and quantity <= 1000. currencyUnits divides any supplied signed cents by 100.0.
hints: Use one final division by 100 for the integer discount.
Use a floating-point division only when converting cents to major units.
